provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Leadership in class
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the duties of a class monitor.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to lead the line properly.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about helping our friends.
Today we learn about being a leader in class.
Content:
A class monitor helps the teacher.
The monitor keeps the classroom tidy.
The monitor leads the line when going out.
The monitor sets a good example for others.
Like when we line up to go to assembly.
Class activity:
Let's take turns being class monitor for one minute.
The monitor will lead the line to the door.
Evaluation questions:
What is the job of a class monitor?
How should you lead the line?
Why is being a leader important?
Summary:
Good leaders help their classmates and follow rules.

topics.title: Following leaders
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to support a class monitor.
The pupils should be able to identify when it is their turn to lead.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about being a class leader.
Today we learn how to follow leaders.
Content:
When someone is leading, we listen to them.
We support our class monitor by following instructions.
We take turns to be leaders too.
Like when we play follow the leader in the playground.
Class activity:
We will play follow the leader game.
Each pupil will get a turn to lead the class.
Evaluation questions:
What should you do when someone is leading?
Why is it good to take turns to lead?
How do you support your class monitor?
Summary:
Good followers listen and help leaders do their job well.

topics.title: Money talk
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to differentiate between needs and wants.
The pupils should be able to explain how to save money.
Introduction:
We see money every day with our parents at the market.
Today we learn about using money wisely.
Content:
Needs are things we must have to live well.
Like food, water and school uniform.
Wants are nice things but we can live without them.
Like toys and extra sweets.
We should buy needs first.
Save money in a piggy bank for later.
Like saving for a new storybook.
Class activity:
Let's sort pictures into needs and wants.
We will make a simple piggy bank from a cardboard box.
Evaluation questions:
What is a need?
What is a want?
How can you save money?
Summary:
Buy needs first and save money for important things.

topics.title: Honesty with money
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify honest actions with money.
The pupils should be able to explain why returning extra change is important.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about buying needs and saving money.
Today we learn about being honest with money.
Content:
Always return extra change to the seller.
Never take money that is not yours.
Like if the market man gives you too much naira.
Tell your teacher if you find money on the ground.
Honest people are trusted by everyone.
Class activity:
Let's play shop with toy naira.
I will give you too much change and see what you do.
Evaluation questions:
What should you do if you get too much change?
Why is it wrong to take money that is not yours?
How does being honest with money make people feel?
Summary:
Always be honest with money and return what is not yours.

topics.title: Good touch, bad touch
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify good and bad touches.
The pupils should be able to explain what to do if someone touches them wrongly.
Introduction:
Our bodies are special and important.
Today we learn about keeping our bodies safe.
Content:
Good touches make you feel happy and safe.
Like hugs from mummy or daddy.
Bad touches make you feel scared or uncomfortable.
No one should touch your private parts.
Your body belongs only to you.
If someone touches you wrongly, shout and tell a trusted adult.
Class activity:
Let's practice shouting "No!" and telling a teacher.
We will point to our private parts under our clothes.
Evaluation questions:
What is a good touch?
What is a bad touch?
What should you do if someone touches you wrongly?
Summary:
Your body is yours and no one should touch you in a bad way.

topics.title: Stranger safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify strangers.
The pupils should be able to explain when it is safe to share your name.
Introduction:
We meet new people every day.
Today we learn how to stay safe with strangers.
Content:
A stranger is someone you do not know well.
Never follow a stranger anywhere.
Even if they offer you sweets or toys.
Only share your name when you are with your parents.
Like at school when your teacher introduces visitors.
Class activity:
We will practice saying "No thank you" to strangers.
We will role - play what to do if a stranger approaches.
Evaluation questions:
Who is a stranger?
Should you follow a stranger? Why?
When is it safe to share your name?
Summary:
Never follow strangers and only share information with trusted adults.

topics.title: Emergency basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify emergency situations.
The pupils should be able to recite their parent's phone number.
Introduction:
Sometimes things happen that need help quickly.
Today we learn what to do in emergencies.
Content:
An emergency is when you need help right away.
Like if you are hurt or lost.
Shout for help loudly so people can hear you.
Know your mummy's or daddy's phone number.
Like if you need them to come pick you up.
Class activity:
Let's practice shouting for help.
We will learn our parent's phone numbers with a song.
Evaluation questions:
What is an emergency?
What should you do in an emergency?
Can you say your parent's phone number?
Summary:
Shout for help and know your parent's phone number in emergencies.

topics.title: Kindness with screens
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why screens need limits.
The pupils should be able to identify what to share with adults about screens.
Introduction:\Phones and tablets are fun but need rules.
Today we learn about being kind with screens.
Content:
Screens need grown up time too.
Like when mummy or daddy is working.
Too much screen time hurts your eyes.
Tell adults what you see on screens.
If something makes you feel scared, tell a teacher.
Class activity:
We will make a screen time chart together.
We will practice telling an adult about something we saw.
Evaluation questions:
Why do screens need grown up time?
What should you do if you see something scary on a screen?
How do screens affect your body?
Summary:
Be kind with screens by following rules and sharing what you see.

topics.title: Peaceful solving
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate peaceful ways to solve problems.
The pupils should be able to explain why talking is better than fighting.
Introduction:
Sometimes we disagree with friends.
Today we learn how to solve problems peacefully.
Content:
When you disagree, talk it out calmly.
Use words like "please" and "thank you".
If you are angry, walk away and cool down.
Agree on a fair solution together.
Like taking turns with a toy.
Class activity:
Let's practice talking out problems with puppets.
We will role - play sharing and taking turns.
Evaluation questions:
What should you do when you disagree with a friend?
Why is talking better than fighting?
How can you agree on a fair solution?
Summary:
Talk problems out and walk away if you feel angry.

topics.title: Revision and safety certificate
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall safety rules learned.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate safe behavior.
Introduction:
We have learned many safety rules this term.
Today we practice what we remember.
Content:
Recall our stranger safety rules.
Remember our honesty with money lessons.
Practice good touch, bad touch knowledge.\Review emergency basics like shouting for help.
Class activity:
We will play safety rules bingo.
Each pupil who remembers well gets a safety star award.
Evaluation questions:
What should you do if a stranger offers you sweets?
How do you keep your body safe?
What is your parent's phone number?
Summary:
Remember all safety rules to stay safe and happy.
